nodes.label: Single-Source Ownership Rule via Service Composition
nodes.community_name: Single-Source Ownership Rule via Service Composition
nodes.norm_label: single-source ownership rule via service composition
nodes.rationale: VisitService composes PatientService and delegates every authorization decision, so the ownership rule lives in exactly one place and cannot drift. It also inherits soft-delete filtering for free. Denormalizing doctor_id onto Visit was rejected because it creates two sources of truth that must stay in sync on patient reassignment, and the problem recurs for every future child resource.

nodes.rationale: Not an access-control gap: because every visit read resolves ownership through get_patient, a soft-deleted patient's visits become immediately unreachable even though their rows keep is_deleted = False. Cleanup is a follow-up.

nodes.label: Client-Side Password Rule
nodes.rationale: 8+ chars with upper, lower, digit and special enforced in the browser — explicitly noted as UX, not security; the backend must enforce the same rule server-side.

nodes.label: Radiology-Viewer Design Aesthetic
nodes.rationale: Dark, high-contrast, monospaced readouts rather than a generic SaaS dashboard, because the primary users are reading MRI-derived data; the confidence gauge is a custom SVG instrument dial deliberately evoking a monitoring display.

nodes.label: Cormorant Garamond Fallback
nodes.rationale: Open-licensed with no restrictions, keeping the same elegant-serif character without a broken-font moment if Seira is not loaded.

nodes.label: IBM Plex Sans UI Font
nodes.rationale: Chosen deliberately over a generic geometric sans because its engineered/data-sheet character reinforces that this is a technical diagnostic tool, and it holds up at small sizes in dense tables. Pairing an elegant serif wordmark against a precise technical interface font is intentional: classy brand mark, clinical product.

nodes.label: Login Screen Spec
nodes.rationale: Structure carried over from the reference design: left panel form, right panel decorative art, with a fixed element order. Only the skin changes. The decorative panel keeps the reference's color family but its stock shapes are to be replaced with neuro motifs so the panel looks like it belongs to this product, not a generic UI kit.

nodes.label: Product Color Palette
nodes.rationale: A calm, light palette for anything a clinician actually works in: bg #EAF3FB, surface #FFFFFF, ink #0F2A43, ink-soft #4B6076, primary #2F6FA6.

nodes.label: Seira Wordmark
nodes.rationale: Used for the logotype only, never body copy or UI labels, because it is a display face not built for small sizes or long text. Free for personal/academic use; a commercial license from Ermedia Studio would be required if the project became commercial. Self-hosted rather than hotlinked.

nodes.norm_label: isolate the redesign rather than modify shared authshell
nodes.rationale: Modifying the shared AuthShell would affect all auth screens, so isolation was chosen at the user's explicit request. The initial shared AuthProvider import produced a duplicate React runtime during server rendering, so the preview now imports only the existing API client, error helper and loginSchema, submitting the same username/password payload while OTP and session handling stay in the original app.

nodes.label: ReportService
nodes.rationale: Composes AnalysisService, VisitService and PatientService rather than querying their tables directly, so a change to any of their authorization rules is inherited automatically.

nodes.label: Database-Free app/ai Package
nodes.rationale: app/ai/ never imports a repository and never touches a Session; it accepts a ClinicalContext and returns an AnalysisResult. The single exception is context.py reading attributes off already-loaded ORM instances, which is the Normalize Input stage. Everything downstream is therefore unit-testable without a database.

nodes.label: Re-Running Analysis Creates a New Row
nodes.norm_label: re-running analysis creates a new row
nodes.rationale: There is no unique constraint on visit_id: re-analysing after adding symptoms is the natural clinician action, and overwriting would destroy prior traceable output. get_latest_for_visit orders by created_at DESC.

nodes.label: Multiple Immutable Reports per Analysis
nodes.rationale: Regenerating creates a new row with a new snapshot, mirroring Analysis never overwriting on visit re-run. There is no 'latest report' endpoint because with multiple reports allowed by design 'latest' is ambiguous in a way 'by analysis_id, newest first' is not.

nodes.label: Render Before Persist
nodes.rationale: ReportService.generate_report builds the snapshot, calls the renderer to prove it produces valid PDF bytes, and only then commits the Report row, so a rendering failure raises before any row exists and no partial Report can be found half-rendered. Same guarantee ADR-003 made for the AI pipeline, applied to a smaller surface.

nodes.label: ReportLab (Platypus) Renderer
nodes.rationale: No new system dependency, a pure-Python-plus-wheel package already validated against Python 3.11. WeasyPrint's Pango/Cairo requirement is a real Windows/Docker cost not worth paying for a two-to-three-page clinical PDF, and a headless-browser render is untestable without a browser in CI. backend/app/reports/renderer.py is a pure function render(snapshot) -> bytes that imports no repository, opens no Session and performs no authorization.

nodes.label: Clinical Context Leaves the Machine
nodes.rationale: A live call sends visit history, symptoms and clinician free text to a third-party API, acceptable only under the unconfirmed synthetic-demo-data assumption. Free tiers may retain or train on submitted data. Pointing live-llm at real patient data requires a security review and is not authorized by this ADR. No prompt or response body may be logged; logging is restricted to model name, latency, HTTP status, visit_id and candidate count.

nodes.label: Prompt-Injection Surface
nodes.rationale: Clinician free text (chief_complaint, history, notes, observation) now reaches a model prompt. Structural mitigations already in place for other reasons contain it: schema validation at the seam, evidence re-resolution, system-authored UUIDs, so the worst realistic outcome is a degraded or dropped candidate. This gets materially worse when real retrieval lands, because a corpus document is a far more attractive injection vector than a symptom field.

nodes.label: Clinician Sign-Off Gates the Report
nodes.rationale: No PDF is produced until a clinician has accepted or amended the analysis, and the report records who signed and when. This makes the safety boundary structural rather than a disclaimer: if an unreviewed AI document can be printed and circulated, the review step is decoration. Adds reviewer identity and timestamp state plus a gate on the PDF endpoint; ADR-004's render-before-persist behaviour is unchanged.

nodes.label: MRI as a Primary Input With Symptoms as Context
nodes.norm_label: mri as a primary input with symptoms as context
nodes.rationale: The documents, not the interface, were stale: the MRI direction is deliberate product intent, so this ADR is the deliberate revision that lifts the V1 exclusion. A visit becomes scan + symptoms + chief complaint at a point in time, consumed by one analysis. Replacing the symptom pipeline would discard a tested backend and the literature-citation differentiator to save UI work.

nodes.label: Dashboard Is a Ranked Triage Queue
nodes.norm_label: dashboard is a ranked triage queue
nodes.rationale: Ordered by open early_watch flags, then worsening trends, then analyses awaiting sign-off. No stat tiles: the queue is itself the answer to 'what needs attention', an aggregate confidence average across patients is clinically meaningless and a step back toward the framing FR-04 warns about, and every tile on the audited dashboard was derived from a hardcoded array. A triage query across all of a clinician's patients cannot be assembled from the existing per-patient routes.

nodes.label: Two Signals Can Disagree
nodes.rationale: Symptoms may point one way and the scan another. Making them one analysis surfaces disagreement as contradicting findings on a candidate rather than two competing verdicts; two independent analyses side by side were rejected because arbitration is the clinical work and handing it over unstructured is worse than one analysis that shows its tensions.

nodes.label: _resolve_evidence Orchestrator Stage
nodes.rationale: A provider is only trusted to select evidence by id, never to be the source of truth for that evidence's content. Re-resolving each document_id against the orchestrator's own retrieval output means a real LLM cannot alter or fabricate citation metadata even if it echoes a document back with different values; only document_id is load-bearing. An unresolvable id raises AIError(ai_contract_error).

nodes.label: RetrievedDocument
nodes.rationale: Carries document_id, chunk_id, source_tier, published_year and relevance_score; typing DiagnosisCandidate.evidence as this full record rather than the narrowed EvidenceRef stops source metadata being silently discarded.

nodes.label: analyses / analysis_findings / analysis_evidence Tables
nodes.rationale: The legacy Diagnosis and Rag stubs are deleted rather than extended. The persisted column is condition_name on analysis_findings; the names final_diagnosis, doctor_verified, probability, certainty and a bare diagnosis are excluded by decision, not oversight.

nodes.label: reports Table
nodes.rationale: Columns: id, analysis_id (FK indexed), generated_by_id (FK to users), generated_at, filename, snapshot (JSONB) plus BaseModel timestamp/soft-delete columns. No pdf_path and no binary PDF column; the empty stub model's design is superseded, not extended.

nodes.label: AI Pipeline Stages
nodes.rationale: Case Data to Normalize to Build Clinical Context to Retrieve Evidence to Rank Evidence to Build AI Context to LLM to Structured Output to Validate to Persist/Return. AI output must use a structured contract rather than unvalidated free-form text.

nodes.label: RAG Rules
nodes.rationale: Accept clinical context, retrieve literature, rank/select evidence, preserve source metadata, supply evidence to the model, attach citations to recommendations. Trusted medical sources are prioritized.

nodes.label: Evidence Scoped to a Finding, Not a Report
nodes.norm_label: evidence scoped to a finding, not a report
nodes.rationale: Citations attach to recommendations, so a report-scoped bag of sources cannot say which condition a citation supports and the mandated chain patient finding + reasoning factor + supporting evidence + citation would be unrepresentable. REPORT-01 reaches evidence via report to analysis to finding to evidence and needs no table of its own.

nodes.label: ReportSnapshot (typed JSONB snapshot)
nodes.rationale: A stored PDF is either wrong twice or a second source of truth to keep consistent with the snapshot. Rendering on every download is cheap at this size and means the download endpoint can never serve stale bytes. It also avoids a PHI-bearing PDF sitting on a container filesystem or in a binary column that a routine backup or log scrape could pick up. A report is read once at generation time and never expected to reflect later edits, so a clinician revising a symptom's severity cannot silently rewrite what a report already said.

nodes.label: Snapshot Duplication and Retention Exposure
nodes.rationale: A snapshot duplicating Analysis/Visit/Patient/Symptom data is the cost of immutability, not an oversight, and means reports inherits the same retention and authorization sensitivity. A retention or right-to-erasure policy will eventually need to reach reports.snapshot; flagged, not solved.

nodes.label: System-Authored trend_basis UUIDs
nodes.rationale: A model that authors UUIDs breaks the premise that a dangling reference means staleness rather than corruption: a fabricated id would be indistinguishable from a stale one and the traceability chain would silently become unfalsifiable. The model names worsening symptoms; the client resolves those names through normalize_symptom_name against context.trends and builds refs from real TrendPoint rows. Same principle as _resolve_evidence: a provider selects, the system resolves.

nodes.label: Scan File Retained Outside the Database
nodes.norm_label: scan file retained outside the database
nodes.rationale: A PDF can be regenerated from its snapshot; a scan cannot. The bytes live in file or object storage with a reference, dimensions and a checksum in the database, keeping ADR-004's no-binary-column rule while accepting that imaging is source data rather than a derived artifact. A storage backend therefore becomes a deployment dependency.

nodes.label: Stage Estimate as Top-Ranked Candidate Only
nodes.norm_label: stage estimate as top-ranked candidate only

nodes.label: DiagnosisCandidate
nodes.rationale: Sets extra="forbid" because a real LLM inventing a field is a contract failure, not a field to ignore. evidence is min_length=1 because a ranked condition with no citation is exactly the untraceable output the traceability rule forbids.

nodes.label: registry.build_providers()
nodes.rationale: A single selection point for provider construction, driven by the AI_PROVIDER config setting, so mock branching never leaks into the orchestrator.

nodes.label: LiveLLMClient
nodes.rationale: Maps LiveCandidatePayload objects into DiagnosisCandidate and resolves symptom names into trend refs. Touches no Session and imports no repository, so the pipeline remains unit-testable without a database. Exceptions are not caught inside it because the orchestrator already maps provider exceptions to the correct AIError codes.

nodes.label: trends.trend_basis_refs() Shared Builder
nodes.rationale: Extracted to app/ai/trends and used by both the mock and live providers so there is one implementation rather than two. trends.py gains an import from app.schemas.analysis for TrendBasisRef with no cycle.

nodes.label: AI Output Contract (Diagnosis structure)
nodes.rationale: Fields: name, category (differential_diagnosis | early_watch), likelihood/confidence, supporting_findings, contradicting_findings, explanation, trend_basis[], evidence[]. Structured rather than free text so validation and traceability are enforceable.

nodes.label: Technology Stack (FastAPI, Pydantic 2, SQLAlchemy, Alembic, PostgreSQL)
nodes.norm_label: technology stack (fastapi, pydantic 2, sqlalchemy, alembic, postgresql)

nodes.label: trend_basis (patient's own visit history)
nodes.rationale: trend_basis traces to the patient's own visit history while evidence[] traces to external literature; the two are distinct and must not be conflated, because conflating internal history with external citation would make the traceability chain meaningless.

nodes.label: Status Colors (status-watch, status-critical, status-stable)
nodes.rationale: Defined early because AI-01's contract already has confidence tiers and an early_watch category. status-watch #D98E04 reuses the brand-amber family so a flag visually ties back to the brand rather than looking like a generic warning color.

nodes.label: early_watch Category Derived From Trend Evidence
nodes.norm_label: early_watch category derived from trend evidence
nodes.rationale: A candidate is early_watch when one of its matched symptoms participates in a worsening multi-visit trend and its confidence is below the differential threshold. Because such a candidate takes its trend_basis from those very trend points, the invariant early_watch implies non-empty trend_basis holds by construction; the schema validator is a second line of defence, not the only one.

nodes.label: trend_basis as a JSON Column
nodes.rationale: It is a snapshot of reasoning, not a live relation: foreign keys would let a later severity edit silently rewrite what a past analysis said, defeating traceability. It is never queried or filtered, only read whole. The UUIDs inside are real visits.id / symptoms.id values but are soft references by design, so a dangling id honestly means the underlying record changed since the analysis ran, which is information rather than corruption.

nodes.label: Two Narrow Protocol Provider Seam
nodes.rationale: Retrieval and reasoning fail differently and are swapped independently, so AI-02 may land a real corpus before a real LLM or vice versa. Splitting them also lets tests inject a failing retriever alongside a healthy LLM to exercise the data-preservation rule precisely. A single combined AIProvider was rejected as coupling two independently swappable concerns.

nodes.label: AI_PROVIDER Defaults to mock
nodes.rationale: Live reasoning is opt-in per environment, and build_providers() raises a configuration error if live-llm is selected without an API key so the failure lands at startup rather than mid-request on a clinician's screen. The mock provider is not deprecated: it keeps the test suite network-free and deterministic. The only irreversible artifact of going live is external, since prompts already sent to a third party cannot be recalled.

nodes.label: category Is Derived, Not Accepted
nodes.rationale: Corrected after the first live call: honouring the model's category made openai/gpt-oss-120b return Parkinson's disease at confidence 0.78 flagged early_watch, which contradicts ADR-003 decision 4 and meant early_watch denoted a low-confidence watch under the mock and any trend-backed finding under a live model. Because category is rendered by the UI and the PDF, which cannot tell which provider produced it, a field whose meaning varies by provider defeats the seam more quietly than one whose type does.

nodes.label: Hosted Model Id Is Not a Stable Identifier
nodes.norm_label: hosted model id is not a stable identifier
nodes.rationale: The first configured default, llama-3.3-70b-versatile, was already retired at first live call and returned 404 model_not_found; the default is now openai/gpt-oss-120b. A model id in configuration is a dependency that can be retired without a release on our side.

nodes.label: LiveCandidatePayload (narrow intermediate schema)
nodes.rationale: Handing a model DiagnosisCandidate.model_json_schema() would be actively harmful: the likelihood_band computed field appears in the serialization schema, a model shown that schema will echo it back, and extra="forbid" then rejects the response, turning deliberate strictness into a self-inflicted failure on every call. The payload carries only what a model should author: evidence_document_ids (ids selected from the supplied list) and trend_symptom_names (names, never UUIDs).

nodes.label: Thin OpenAI-Compatible LLM Client
nodes.rationale: The wire format is the commodity: Groq, OpenRouter, Gemini's compatibility endpoint, Together, Ollama and OpenAI all speak the same /chat/completions shape, so one ~50-line client covers every provider without a per-vendor code branch. A vendor SDK would buy typed errors at the cost of pinning the project to one vendor's release cadence. AI_LLM_BASE_URL + AI_LLM_MODEL + AI_LLM_API_KEY select the provider; the only new dependency is httpx==0.28.1.

nodes.label: Test Suite Pinned to the Mock Provider
nodes.norm_label: test suite pinned to the mock provider
nodes.rationale: Several suites call build_providers() with no argument, reading the real Settings; with a second AI_PROVIDER value a developer whose backend/.env selected live-llm had the suite issue real model calls, observed as ten tests hitting Groq and tripling run time. tests/conftest.py now sets AI_PROVIDER=mock in the environment, which outranks the .env file; live-provider tests build their own Settings and drive an httpx.MockTransport.

nodes.label: Staging Model Behind Its Own Provider Seam
nodes.norm_label: staging model behind its own provider seam
nodes.rationale: A third seam alongside the retriever and the reasoning client, following the pattern that has now worked twice: schema-real, provider-mocked, deterministic, labelled as simulated. Because provenance is now three-dimensional (simulated retrieval, live reasoning, simulated staging), AI_PROVIDER as a single literal no longer stretches and staging needs its own setting.

nodes.label: Client to API to Service to Repository Layering
nodes.norm_label: client to api to service to repository layering

nodes.label: Deployment Partial (compose runs, no scan volume)
nodes.norm_label: deployment partial (compose runs, no scan volume)

nodes.label: Scan Storage Not Durable in Container
nodes.norm_label: scan storage not durable in container

nodes.label: AnalysisRepository.create_with_status
nodes.rationale: One commit writes analysis + findings + evidence + visit.status=ANALYZED, and is the single place VisitStatus.ANALYZED is written.

nodes.label: Server-Side Audit Logging of the Real Reason
nodes.norm_label: server-side audit logging of the real reason
nodes.rationale: The 404 is a caller-facing signal only, not a logging decision: logs must still capture ownership violation vs true absence for audit and debugging.

nodes.label: MAX_CONFIDENCE Ceiling of 0.92
nodes.rationale: Confidence is clamped so output never expresses certainty; likelihood, never certainty.

nodes.label: Enumeration Resistance for PHI-Adjacent Resources
nodes.rationale: Which response the API gives is itself a small information disclosure; enumeration resistance matters more for a UUID-keyed resource tied to a real patient than for a low-sensitivity resource.

nodes.label: Ownership Violations Return 404, Not 403
nodes.rationale: Patients are PHI-adjacent, so a 403 confirming record existence to an unauthorized caller is an information-disclosure and enumeration surface not worth the marginal honesty benefit to someone who mistyped an ID. A uniform 404 across true-absence and ownership-violation means client code never special-cases which kind of 404 it received.

nodes.label: 404 Re-Labelling / Identifier Masking
nodes.rationale: A 404 is labelled with the resource the caller actually named. Letting a Patient-shaped EntityNotFoundError propagate on /visits/{id} would disclose the parent patient's UUID — an ADR-001 violation wearing a 404's clothing. Masking is about not disclosing identifiers the caller did not supply, so patient-scoped routes keep the honest Patient label.

nodes.label: Symptom-Belongs-To-Visit Verification
nodes.rationale: _load_authorized_symptom asserts symptom.visit_id == visit.id; without it, /visits/{A}/symptoms/{belongs-to-B} would silently edit a symptom on a different case. A mismatched pair reads as a missing symptom.

nodes.label: Failure Precedes the First Write
nodes.rationale: Every read and every provider call happens before the first write, so when a failure occurs there is nothing to roll back and no recovery path to get wrong. Ordering is a stronger guarantee than exception handling: a try/except around a partially-completed write would satisfy the letter of the rule while leaving a window the ordering approach does not have.

nodes.label: A Failed Run Persists Nothing
nodes.rationale: Persisting FAILED analysis rows would add an enum and a migration hazard to represent something logging already covers, and risks a failed run being read as clinical output. Failure telemetry is logging with visit id only, never patient data.

nodes.label: Rule-Based Deterministic Mock Scoring
nodes.rationale: No RNG and no canned results: the score is arithmetic over what the clinician actually entered, ordered by (-confidence, name) so ties are total and reproducible. Seeded RNG is stable but arbitrary and cannot make an early_watch point at a real trend; golden fixtures do not respond to input, so ranking and validation would never execute and the demo would answer identically regardless of input.

nodes.label: Filenames Carry No PHI
nodes.rationale: neuroone-report-{report_id}.pdf. The report id is generated in the service rather than left to a database default so the filename is available before the row is constructed.

nodes.label: reports Has No Owner Column
nodes.rationale: analysis_id already resolves to exactly one owning clinician through the analysis to visit to patient chain, and a second independent authorization path would eventually drift from the first. Re-deriving through AnalysisService means a Report's authorization is exactly as correct as Analysis's already-tested authorization. A Report reached by its own id 404s as Report, not as Analysis or Visit.

nodes.label: Determinism Lost on the Live Path
nodes.norm_label: determinism lost on the live path
nodes.rationale: No equivalent to the mock's byte-identical-JSON guarantee exists or can exist for a live model; get_latest_for_visit ordering by created_at DESC already accommodates re-runs producing different candidates.

nodes.label: Hard/Soft Failure Line for Model Output
nodes.norm_label: hard/soft failure line for model output
nodes.rationale: Structural violations fail hard; per-candidate content violations are normalized or dropped. A malformed envelope means the provider is broken, while one over-confident or uncited candidate among five means the model was imprecise about one row. Raising on the latter destroys an otherwise-good analysis and, because every failure precedes the first write, costs the clinician the whole run. Dropping is not lenient: a dropped candidate never reaches the database and an unresolved citation is discarded rather than persisted.

nodes.label: UI Copy Prohibition on Certainty Language
nodes.norm_label: ui copy prohibition on certainty language

nodes.label: PatientService._authorize_access
nodes.rationale: Raises the same EntityNotFoundError for 'doesn't exist' and 'exists but not yours' so API call sites need not distinguish them.

nodes.label: Coding Standards (type hints, PEP 8, services own business logic)
nodes.norm_label: coding standards (type hints, pep 8, services own business logic)

nodes.label: Feature → API → Service → Repository → Model → Schema Flow
nodes.norm_label: feature → api → service → repository → model → schema flow

nodes.label: Per-Record Ownership Check
nodes.rationale: A CLINICIAN may only access patients where patient.doctor_id == current_user.id; an ADMIN is unrestricted. Scoped narrowly to per-record checks, deliberately distinct from role-level exclusion.

nodes.label: require_roles Role-Level 403 Signaling
nodes.rationale: Role-level exclusions continue to use 403 because there is no record-existence information to protect: the caller already knows the endpoint exists.

nodes.label: detect_trends Must Be Extended for Scan Metrics
nodes.norm_label: detect_trends must be extended for scan metrics
nodes.rationale: It reads symptom severities today; unless scan-derived metrics feed it, the trend story stays symptom-only and the scan contributes nothing to early_watch.

nodes.label: Centralized Domain-to-HTTP Error Translation
nodes.rationale: Domain exceptions stay independent of HTTP concerns; one central handler maps validation, auth, not-found, conflict, database, AI and external-service errors to HTTP responses.

nodes.label: Initial Domain Entities (User, Patient, Clinical Case/Visit, Diagnosis, Evidence, Report)
nodes.norm_label: initial domain entities (user, patient, clinical case/visit, diagnosis, evidence, report)

nodes.label: JWT Authentication Flow
nodes.rationale: Authentication dependencies expose overridable service providers rather than constructing services directly inside request dependencies, so tests and alternate wiring can substitute them.

nodes.label: Layered Architecture (API to Service to Repository to PostgreSQL)
nodes.norm_label: layered architecture (api to service to repository to postgresql)
nodes.rationale: API does HTTP routing/validation/serialization with no business logic; Services own business rules, authorization decisions and repository/AI coordination; Repositories do persistence only with no HTTP logic. Separation keeps domain exceptions independent of HTTP concerns.

nodes.label: Role-Based Authorization (ADMIN, CLINICIAN)
nodes.rationale: Access control is enforced server-side at API/service boundaries rather than trusted to the client.

nodes.label: Intake Splits Into New Patient and New Visit
nodes.norm_label: intake splits into new patient and new visit
nodes.rationale: Patient creation takes demographics only, matching the real PatientCreate contract; visit creation takes scan, symptoms and complaint. The previous single combined form could not express 'an existing patient returns for a follow-up scan', which is the only case that produces a trend. The current upload page posts multipart/form-data with mri_scan, mmse_score and family_history to POST /patients, which accepts PatientCreate JSON, so it cannot ever have worked and must be rebuilt rather than adapted.

nodes.label: Scan Attaches to a Visit, Not a Patient
nodes.norm_label: scan attaches to a visit, not a patient
nodes.rationale: Cross-visit scan comparison then costs nothing structurally because detect_trends already consumes per-visit data and visit ownership rules already exist. The USP is a trajectory, and a trajectory needs more than one point; one current scan per patient removes the second data point early detection requires.

nodes.label: ADR-002 — Visit Ownership Derives From Parent Patient
nodes.norm_label: adr-002 — visit ownership derives from parent patient

nodes.label: AI Pipeline Contract Complete, Providers Simulated
nodes.norm_label: ai pipeline contract complete, providers simulated

nodes.label: Dashboard Not Started Against Real Data
nodes.norm_label: dashboard not started against real data

nodes.label: Explainable AI in the API, Not the UI
nodes.norm_label: explainable ai in the api, not the ui

nodes.label: Backend Complete for the MVP Journey
nodes.norm_label: backend complete for the mvp journey

nodes.label: Milestone 2 Connect the Frontend in Vertical Slices
nodes.norm_label: milestone 2 connect the frontend in vertical slices

nodes.label: pipeline_note Provenance Label
nodes.rationale: Mock-sourced output must stay labelled 'pipeline complete, evidence retrieval simulated' because a mocked pipeline returning schema-valid output looks real in a demo; the mitigation is ultimately narrative, not technical.

nodes.label: Clinical Safety Boundary (NeuroONE assists, never autonomously diagnoses)
nodes.norm_label: clinical safety boundary (neuroone assists, never autonomously diagnoses)
nodes.rationale: Not negotiable and not revised by this ADR. FR-04's prohibition on definitive-diagnosis framing continues to apply to the stage estimate, reaching schema, API field naming, UI copy and the PDF. Uploaded diagnostic-report analysis, autonomous diagnosis and automated treatment decisions remain hard exclusions; admitting MRI is not a precedent for admitting the others.

nodes.label: HYBRID_PIPELINE_NOTE
nodes.rationale: With a live LLM and a mocked retriever, the old expression would stamp 'evidence retrieved from live corpus' onto an analysis whose evidence came from mock_corpus.py, disabling the one technical mitigation on record at the exact moment it starts mattering. Selection now reads retriever.provenance alongside reasoning.provider_mode. ADR-003's prediction about not touching the orchestrator is knowingly broken because honest labelling outranks a prediction about file scope.

nodes.label: provider_mode Is Not Widened to hybrid
nodes.norm_label: provider_mode is not widened to hybrid
nodes.rationale: It is persisted on analyses.provider_mode and exposed on AnalysisResponse, so a third member means a migration, a wire-contract change for the frontend and REPORT-01, and a new state every consumer must learn. pipeline_note is already a free-text field carried on every analysis for exactly this purpose.

nodes.label: Provenance Stated per Analysis, Not per Environment
nodes.norm_label: provenance stated per analysis, not per environment
nodes.rationale: Each analysis carries a line derived from pipeline_note describing what was real and what was simulated, travelling into the PDF, so a screenshot of a result cannot be mistaken for validated clinical output. A persistent environment-level demo banner was rejected because it says nothing about which parts of a specific result were simulated. A staging UI backed by a mocked model is more convincing than a mocked text pipeline, because a brain region with a percentage looks like measurement, so this mitigation is not optional.

nodes.label: Stage Estimate as Top-Ranked Candidate, Never a Lone Verdict
nodes.norm_label: stage estimate as top-ranked candidate, never a lone verdict
nodes.rationale: A stage label is a conclusion; a ranked differential with contradicting findings is decision support. Output stays a ranked list with likelihood bands, supporting and contradicting findings, and citations. CN / MCI / Mild / Moderate / Severe may appear as the highest-ranked candidate but not as a single headline answer with a certainty figure, and the word 'certainty' does not appear in UI copy.

nodes.label: Contributing Regions Visualization Has No API
nodes.norm_label: contributing regions visualization has no api

nodes.label: Mocked Staging Model Reads as Measurement
nodes.norm_label: mocked staging model reads as measurement

nodes.label: Report Preview Page Has No API
nodes.norm_label: report preview page has no api

nodes.label: Sign-Off Is a Gate, Not a Status
nodes.norm_label: sign-off is a gate, not a status

nodes.label: Sign in via OTP Button Replaces Google Sign-In
nodes.norm_label: sign in via otp button replaces google sign-in
nodes.rationale: The secondary button submits the existing form through its HTML form association, preserving validation, pending state, error handling and credential-to-OTP handoff. No passwordless endpoint, backend change or auth contract change is introduced. This follow-up supersedes the original Google/register layout requirement.
